blocks.text: Daniel removed the tank’s long gun and left it on blocks beside the workbench.
By noon, the Army ray occupied its place.
blocks.alt: Dork tightens the mounting plate around the shrink ray’s copper emitter in the tank turret, while Jaws watches from clear air above.

blocks.text: The gray box sat inside the turret, held by brackets. Its copper-ringed barrel projected through a square plate where the gun had been. Daniel tightened the last bolt, tugged the mounting and climbed down to inspect it from the floor.
Jaws floated above the turret.
“Much better.”
Daniel agreed.
He had locked the turret facing forward. A cable ran down to a firing switch beside the driver’s seat. To aim, he would turn the tank. To fire, he would stop.
He checked the blue setting once more.
Laura waited by the loading doors. Behind her, the stolen vault stood open. Most of the money remained on its shelves; Daniel had tucked several bundles into a drawer.
He climbed into the forward hatch.
The engine coughed, caught and filled the workshop with a heavy rumble.
Laura raised the door.
The first officer saw the tank turn toward Public Square and reached for his radio.
Traffic had already stopped. A delivery driver left his truck at the curb. Pedestrians backed away from the crossing as the tracks ground around the corner.
Daniel steered between the abandoned vehicles.
Laura walked beside him. Jaws drifted ahead, grinning at the people who hurried out of his way.
The tank stopped short of the square.
Daniel rose just far enough through the driver’s hatch to lift a battery megaphone.
“This city will obey Daniel Orkleson.”
A bus driver opened both doors. People spilled onto the sidewalk.
Daniel pointed toward Terminal Tower.
“Or I’ll take that home.”
He lowered himself into the tank.
The megaphone stayed on the lip of the hatch.
Two police cars pulled across the street ahead. Officers stepped out, calling for people to get behind the buildings. One waved a busload of passengers toward a side street.
Laura watched them begin to spread out.
Beside the curb stood a renovation skip, broken packing boards piled along its edge. She spat a bright shot into the dry wood.
blocks.alt: Laura ignites discarded packing boards beside Public Square as Dork’s modified tank blocks the street and officers fall back.

blocks.text: Flame raced through the splinters.
She moved along the pile, lighting another section, then sent a shot across the road into discarded cardboard beside a work barrier. Heat and smoke closed the direct approach to the tank.
An officer trying to pass between the fires caught sight of her.
Laura took aim at the pavement in front of him.
He retreated.
Behind her, the tank’s engine rose. One track moved farther than the other, swinging the short copper barrel toward the police cars.
The officers saw it turn.
“Clear the cars!”
They ran for the stone corner of a building.
Daniel stopped the tank.
Blue light crossed the street.
blocks.alt: A blue shot from the tank’s turret strikes an empty police cruiser while a previously shrunken cruiser sits beside the curb.

blocks.text: The first empty cruiser dwindled on its tires. Its roof sank below the curb, its flashing light becoming a pinprick. In a moment it sat in the roadway no bigger than a toy.
The second car vanished behind another blue flash.
It was still there when the light cleared, small enough to lift in one hand.
Daniel leaned toward his viewing slit.
The roadblock had left him plenty of room.
Jaws swooped around the smoke before the officers could regroup.
blocks.alt: The bodyless Jaws chases two officers past a stone planter, his steel teeth snapping as they retreat from the tank.

blocks.text: His metal teeth snapped shut beside a policeman’s sleeve. The officer jerked away and stumbled toward the sidewalk. His partner caught his arm.
Jaws followed.
They ducked behind a stone planter. He came over the top, jaws opening wide.
Both men scrambled away.
He chased them as far as the next doorway, laughing through his steel teeth, then wheeled back toward the tank. Laura’s fires still burned between the scattered police positions.
Daniel brought the megaphone up again.
“Now. Who’s in charge?”
Nobody stepped into the street.
Billy heard the first report at the facility desk.
Tank. Public Square. Officers requesting assistance.
He was already off the chair when the next voice mentioned the blue light.
Seth and Jenny came through from the window. Fist followed them.
Billy tapped the four newspaper clippings, then pointed to the square on his street atlas. Seth bent over the map while Jenny listened to the radio.
A third report came through: cars reduced in size, officers forced back by fire.
Billy wrote it down exactly as reported. In the margin he added: Army: “for transport.” He would be having a word with the Army about their definition of transport.
Billy marked the blocked street with his pencil.
The western approach remained open.
He called the police contact from that morning, identified himself and passed on the route. People needed to leave by the side streets, away from the tank’s front. The Defenders were coming.
Then he tore the marked page from his notebook and put it in his coat pocket.
Jenny reached the door first.
Seth paused beside the desk. Through the open window, the room still held its ordinary afternoon sounds.
He looked once toward the sky.
Then he went after her.
At Public Square, Daniel eased the tank past the two tiny cruisers.
Laura kept to its left. Jaws hovered above the pavement on its right, watching the doorways.
Beyond the smoke, Terminal Tower rose over the square.
Daniel corrected his steering.
The copper barrel settled toward the building.
